name: How Do You Know If a Remodel Timeline Is Unrealistic?

mainEntity.name: How can I tell if a kitchen renovation contractor is overpromising on the schedule?
mainEntity.text: How can I tell if a kitchen renovation contractor is overpromising on the schedule?

acceptedAnswer.text: An overpromised schedule usually sounds effortless. If the contractor says the job will move quickly without discussing permits, inspections, cabinet lead times, or material availability, that is a warning sign. Kitchen remodels involve multiple dependent steps, and each one can affect the next. A realistic contractor will explain what must happen before demolition, what happens after rough trades, when inspections are needed, and how long finish materials may take to arrive. They should also explain what can cause delays and how those delays are communicated. In Los Angeles County, even well-run projects can be affected by permit review or inspection scheduling. Ask for a schedule that includes milestones rather than just a single completion date. That lets you see whether the contractor understands the actual workflow. A trustworthy schedule is specific, sequenced, and tied to real-world constraints instead of optimistic guesses.
acceptedAnswer.description: Warning signs include a very fast timeline, vague sequencing, no mention of permits or inspections, and promises that materials will always be available immediately. A realistic contractor explains dependencies, lead times, and possible delays. If the schedule sounds too good to be true, it probably is.
